title: Windows 95 Startup
blurb: Microsoft commissioned this from Brian Eno with a brief asking for something inspiring, universal and optimistic — and, famously, a hard length limit of three and a quarter seconds. He made eighty-four versions before settling. The one that shipped in 1995 opens on that shimmering major chord and remains the most artful piece of music any operating system has ever booted with. For anybody who owned a beige tower it is pure sense-memory: dial-up in the next room, a CRT warming up, an entire afternoon still ahead.
origin: The Windows 95 startup sound, composed by Brian Eno (1995).
